messages.subject: Data structure and import of data
parts:
Hello to everyone, I am working with birds and this is the first time I am using the Distance Software. I have 3 different habitats with 2 line transects to each of them. I was collecting the data for almost 2 months. I want to ask the followings:

1. The effort will be the distance of the line multiply by the replicates?
2.How I will structure the data? Could someone show me an example of single observer line transect data look like in the software?
3. I have to enter also the replicates with no observations?
4. If a replicates had 2 or 3 observations how it will look like at the data table?

Thanks for your time and looking forward for a reply!

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Data structure and import of data
parts:
Stylianos

Sorry for the delayed response; we were teaching a distance sampling workshop last week.

If you look in the Users Guide for Distance, that came with Distance (go to Help | Users Guide), look at Chapter 5 "Data in Distance".  On page 53 of the Guide that ships with Distance 7.1, you will see this input file for import into Distance:

That will get you started for the basic form of the file that you will import.  Lines 1A and 1B each have 3 detections, line 2B has 4 detections and line 1B has NO detections.

In answer to your specific questions, if you walked the transects more than once, then the effort for the transect is the length multiplied by the number of times walked.  If a visit has no detections, the effort multiplier remains the number of times walked.  I hope that gets you started on your data entry.

Next time you conduct your study, try to have more than two transects per habitat.  You will need more spatial replication to obtain a defensible estimate of variability in encounter rate between transects.
